title: Rename offset fields to *Char to honestly represent UTF-16 code units, not bytes
context: Fields computed via JS string indexing (.length, .indexOf(), regex .index) yield UTF-16 code unit offsets, not UTF-8 byte offsets. The field names (startByte/endByte/atByte) misrepresented this, risking bugs if callers assumed true byte positions.
decision: Renamed startByte/endByte/atByte → startChar/endChar/atChar in helm.ts and k8sManifest.ts. Created distinct HelmSymbol/HelmCall types (instead of reusing ParsedSymbol/ParsedCall) to encapsulate honest naming. Annotated the merge in indexer.ts to explicitly map char offsets into the shared arrays' startByte/endByte fields (which also carry char values in practice per issue #84).
consequences: API contract now accurately represents what units offsets use, preventing misinterpretation
Explicitly documents the UTF-16 vs UTF-8 distinction at extraction and merge boundaries
Requires type mapping at the merge point (helm/k8s extractors → shared symbol/call arrays)
Distinguishes extractor-specific types from the shared ParsedSymbol/ParsedCall format
alternatives_rejected: Convert to actual UTF-8 byte offsets — expensive re-indexing for no practical gain given JS string APIs
Keep misleading names and add comments — doesn't fix the API contract, still confusing to future callers
Leave as-is — silently risks bugs when someone relies on 'byte' semantics that were never true
